text: Everything so far has lived in Power BI Desktop, refreshing only when you click Refresh yourself. The Sales Director asked for a report that updates on its own before Monday's meeting, and that only happens in the Power BI Service.

Four real steps get you there. Publish the report from Desktop to a workspace. Install the On-premises Data Gateway, the bridge that lets the cloud Service reach your local SQL Server. Register the data source on that gateway, with credentials that can read the three staged views. Then bind the dataset to that gateway data source and configure the schedule.

The gateway isn't optional here. AdventureWorks2012 runs on a SQL Server instance the Power BI Service simply cannot reach on its own. Without the gateway, the Schedule refresh option either won't appear or will fail with a connection error every single time it runs. This is one of the most common real-world blockers teams hit the first time they try this.

Turn scheduled refresh on, set it to weekly, Sunday at six PM, so the numbers are fresh before Monday's meeting. And add a failure notification email, so a broken refresh doesn't sit unnoticed until someone asks why the report looks stale.

Before trusting the schedule unattended, trigger one manual refresh to confirm the gateway path actually works. Next lesson: remember that Total Sales number you noted on the Drill-Down page back in Lesson 8? It's time to compare it against the Executive Summary page.
